title: R9 v3: orchestrator/allocation.py — critical-path-aware executor allocation by expected value with class-scoped economics, pinned input shapes, hard eligibility and evidence thresholds (AP P16)
spec:
Why: pool.pick_executor (orchestrator/pool.py:538-559) picks the cheapest proven-safe executor by class economics and ignores scheduling importance; AP P16 / brief P11 want executor choice that weighs expected accepted-task cost, first-pass success, fix-round cost, duration and critical-path importance, never "critical path = strongest model". v3 after spec reviews T-0617 and T-0628: economics class-scoped, input shapes pinned, no reference to fields executor_economics does not produce.
What: new pure module orchestrator/allocation.py; the hook into executor.start is a later integration task. Tests are unittest.TestCase methods.
- cfg [allocation]: mode off|shadow|active (default shadow; unknown -> shadow), min_samples 5, latency_weight_usd_per_hour 2.0, critical_factor 1.0, non_critical_factor 0.25.
- evidence_for(executor_ids, task_class, *, economics=None, root=STATE) -> {executor_id: {"cost_to_accepted_usd", "first_pass_p", "expected_rework_usd", "n"}}: economics defaults to scorecard.executor_economics(root=root, by="class"), whose rows are keyed by the tuple (executor_id, task_class) (scorecard.py: key = (executor_id, root_row[by])); for each id read the row for (id, task_class): cost_to_accepted_usd = row["cost_to_accepted"], first_pass_p = 1 - row["fix_round_probability"] (deliberately not first_pass_green_rate: fix_round_probability is defined over every resolved lineage and so has broader coverage; state this in the docstring), expected_rework_usd = row["cost_to_accepted"] * row["fix_round_probability"] when both are not None else None (executor_economics has no initial-vs-fix-round split; this proxy is the expected rework share of the accepted cost, stated in the docstring), n = row["n_tasks"]; a missing tuple key yields all None and n 0.
- choose(task, eligible_ids, *, baseline, priority, ready_priorities, evidence, durations=None, cfg=None) -> {"executor", "mode", "reason", "candidates": [{id, score_usd, cost_to_accepted_usd, first_pass_p, est_duration_s, n, measured}], "rejected": {id: reason}, "baseline", "would_pick"}. Shapes: priority = critical_path.explain dict for this task; ready_priorities = list[float] of critical_path_s values of every ready task (this task included); durations = dict[executor_id, float] of this task's estimated seconds under each executor, precomputed by the caller, optional; est_duration_s falls back to critical_path.est_duration_s(task). factor = critical_factor when priority["critical_path_s"] >= max(ready_priorities) else non_critical_factor. score_usd = cost_to_accepted_usd + latency_weight_usd_per_hour x est_duration_s / 3600 x factor. measured = n >= min_samples and cost_to_accepted_usd is not None. Fewer than two measured candidates -> executor = baseline, reason "sparse_evidence". Ties within 5 percent of score -> lower cost_to_accepted_usd, then baseline, then id. Never returns an id outside eligible_ids; eligible_ids empty -> None with reason "no_eligible"; baseline not in eligible_ids -> ValueError. mode off -> baseline, reason mode_off, would_pick None; shadow -> executor = baseline, would_pick = EV choice; active -> executor = EV choice.
- record(task_id, result) -> decision_log.record(kind="allocation", subject=task_id, candidates=ids, hard_constraints=["eligibility"] (capacity and budget are enforced upstream by pool.eligible_executors and are inherited context, not verified here; say so in the docstring), deterministic={"baseline": baseline}, historical=evidence, selected=result["executor"], rejected=result["rejected"], reason=result["reason"], n=min n over measured, mode).
acceptance: tests/test_allocation.py::test_evidence_for_is_scoped_to_the_task_class — economics rows keyed (executor, class) for two classes yield per-executor evidence from the requested class only, a missing tuple gives None values and n 0, first_pass_p equals 1 - fix_round_probability and expected_rework_usd equals cost_to_accepted x fix_round_probability

tests/test_allocation.py::test_cheap_executor_preferred_when_outcomes_equivalent — two measured executors with equal first-pass and duration but costs 0.5 and 1.5 USD: active mode picks the cheaper one

tests/test_allocation.py::test_stronger_executor_only_when_downstream_value_justifies — on a critical-path task the executor with duration 600 s and cost 1.2 beats duration 2400 s and cost 0.8; on a non-critical task with non_critical_factor the cheaper one wins
tests/test_allocation.py::test_hard_eligibility_always_wins — the best-scoring executor absent from eligible_ids is never returned; empty eligible_ids returns None with reason no_eligible
tests/test_allocation.py::test_sparse_evidence_falls_back_to_baseline — only one candidate meets min_samples: executor is baseline with reason sparse_evidence

tests/test_allocation.py::test_modes_and_decision_row — off returns baseline with mode_off; shadow returns baseline and would_pick; record writes an allocation decision row with candidates, selected and rejected

constraints.interface_contract: evidence_for(executor_ids, task_class, *, economics=None, root=STATE) -> {id: {cost_to_accepted_usd, first_pass_p, expected_rework_usd, n}} from executor_economics(by='class') tuple keys; choose(task, eligible_ids, *, baseline, priority, ready_priorities: list[float], evidence, durations: dict[executor_id, float]|None = None, cfg=None) -> {executor, mode, reason, candidates, rejected, baseline, would_pick}; record(task_id, result) writes decision_log kind allocation; config [allocation] mode off|shadow|active default shadow, min_samples 5, latency_weight_usd_per_hour 2.0, critical_factor 1.0, non_critical_factor 0.25; must not import daemon or executor
